introduction: This spec makes the `af` binary a client of the agent-fox service. A person stores a hub credential with `af login`, then subscribes hub workspaces, queues triage and fix jobs (`--workspace`), follows a job until it is at rest, and lists, answers, retries and cancels jobs. Every command speaks the existing one-envelope contract. Running the loops on the person's own machine is still available, and now needs an explicit `--local`.

glossary.at rest: A job whose state is `blocked`, `done`, `failed` or `cancelled` and none of whose attempts is `running`.
glossary.credential file: `~/.af/config.toml`, the file `afc login` writes. Its top-level string key `token` is the only source of the hub credential.
glossary.failed try: A try that ends without the job at rest and delivers no new event.
glossary.from the flag: Said of a server that `--server` named rather than `AF_URL`. Such a server's suggested argv entries (`next`, `resume.argv`) then carry `--server <url>`.
glossary.job result: The result `{job, envelope}` shared by every job command. `job` is the service's job document carried verbatim, and `envelope` is the final attempt's stored envelope or null.
glossary.local mode: `af triage` or `af fix` run with `--local`: the loop runs on this machine exactly as before this spec.
glossary.server: The agent-fox service base URL. It comes from `--server`, or else from `AF_URL`. The API lives at `<server>/api/v1/…`.
glossary.service command: Any command that sends requests to the agent-fox service: `af login`, `af workspace …`, `af jobs …`, and `af triage`/`af fix` in service mode.
glossary.service mode: `af triage` or `af fix` run with `--workspace <slug>`: a job is queued on the agent-fox service and no loop runs on this machine.
glossary.try: One request to `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/events?since=<n>` and, once that stream ends, one read of `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}`.
glossary.workspace PAT: The hub token that `af workspace subscribe` reads from `--hub-token-file` and sends to the service as `hub_token`.

requirements.title: Choosing where a triage or fix runs
requirements.rationale: A guessed mode would send a person's report to the wrong place, and a refused invocation must leave no trace.

criteria.condition: `af triage` or `af fix` is invoked on the af binary's command line with neither `--local` nor `--workspace`
criteria.action: refuse the invocation with a usage error. Its message says to choose and names `--workspace <slug>` (on the service that `--server` or `AF_URL` names) and `--local`
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2; `error.fix_hint` is `{flag: "--workspace"}` when a server is named and `{flag: "--local"}` otherwise

criteria.condition: `af triage` or `af fix` is invoked with both `--local` and `--workspace`
criteria.action: refuse the invocation with a usage error that names both flags
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.action: choose the mode of `af triage` and `af fix` before it parses flags for a mode, resolves the input, builds a forge client, creates a run directory or sends any request. An invocation refused by 16-REQ-1 or 16-REQ-2 therefore sends no request to the service or the forge and creates no `.agent-fox/run/` directory
read only the words after the command path and before the first `--`, and treat any word after `--` as the input, never as a mode
treat a word that is the value of a value-taking flag of either mode as that flag's value and never as a mode. So `af triage x --context --local` names no mode and exits 2

accept each mode flag with one dash or two. `--workspace <slug>` and `--workspace=<slug>` both choose service mode, and a `--workspace` with no value or an empty value is a usage error naming `--workspace`
criteria.contract: a missing or empty `--workspace` value gives status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.action: read `--local` as a Go boolean flag: `--local` and `--local=true` choose local mode, `--local=false` counts as not given, and a value that `strconv.ParseBool` refuses is a usage error naming `--local`
criteria.contract: an unparseable `--local` value gives status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.condition: a person runs `af triage --help`, `af help triage`, `af fix --help` or `af help fix`
criteria.action: print help that describes both local mode and service mode, with each mode's flags
criteria.contract: exit code 0

requirements.title: Mode-specific flags, local-mode compatibility, schemas and documentation
requirements.rationale: A flag that silently does nothing is worse than a refusal, and local runs must keep behaving exactly as before.

criteria.condition: local mode is chosen and `--server` or `--wait` is given
criteria.action: refuse the invocation with a usage error that names the refused flag
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2; no forge read, no request and no run directory

criteria.condition: service mode is chosen and a flag only the loop reads is given. For both commands these are `--dir`, `--repo`, `--dry-run`, `--land`, `--brain`, `--sandbox`, `--borrowed-hands`, `--budget`, `--max-turns` and `--script`; for triage, `--label`; for fix, `--base`, `--attempts` and `--no-verify`
criteria.action: refuse the invocation with a usage error that names the refused flag
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2; no request is sent

criteria.action: accept `--context`, `--timeout`, `--output` and `--emit-events` on `af triage` and `af fix` in both modes
criteria.contract: none of these four flags gives a usage error in either mode

criteria.condition: local mode is chosen
criteria.action: run `af triage` and `af fix` with the same flags, defaults, input resolution, forge client, run directory, events, warnings, results, statuses, exit codes and envelopes as before this spec, even when `AF_URL` points at a closed port. No request is sent to any agent-fox service
criteria.contract: for the same input and flags, the envelope equals the pre-spec envelope. The one exception is the fix suggestion of 16-REQ-2.5

criteria.condition: triage reaches a confirmed or probable diagnosis, either from the loop or from `af triage land`
criteria.action: add to `next` the argv `af fix <issue url> --dir <dir> --local`, so that the suggestion runs as given
criteria.contract: `next[].argv` equals `["af","fix",<issue url>,"--dir",<dir>,"--local"]`

criteria.action: apply the mode rule only to the af binary's command line. An in-process caller of the loops, such as the worker of `13_agent_fox_worker`, runs them without `--local` and never sends a request to an agent-fox service
criteria.contract: 13_agent_fox_worker's tests pass unchanged

criteria.action: register a result schema for every new command. The schemas for the job result `{job, envelope}`, the job page, the subscription view, `{workspaces}`, `{slug}` and `{credential_file, server}` describe the fields `af` relies on and allow other fields. `af triage --schema` and `af fix --schema` admit both the local result and the job result
criteria.contract: `cmd/af/testdata/schema.golden.json` is regenerated and matches `--schema` output byte for byte

criteria.action:
document the following, all checked by a docs test:
- in `docs/cli.md`: the mode rule and how its words are read; the new commands and flags; the order of local checks and the answer table; the categories `service`, `conflict`, `hub` and `job_cancelled`, with `cancelled` still a signal sent to the process; the warnings `server_insecure`, `credential_file_permissions` and `attempt_envelope_unavailable`; the event `job_event`; that a command may supply its own `resume.argv`; the triage and fix synopses with `--local`; `af fix <issue url> --dir <dir> --local`; the count of registered commands
- in `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/model-usage.md`: `AF_URL`, `~/.af/config.toml` and its `token` key, and that a job's cost is `result.job.usage`
- the client in `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/development.md` and `README.md`
Every divergence is recorded in `docs/errata/16_*.md`, and no phrase an existing docs test checks is removed
criteria.contract: `make check` passes offline

requirements.title: Naming the service
requirements.rationale: The service is named only by `--server` or `AF_URL`. A URL that could leak a password, or send a credential in clear, must be caught.

criteria.action: take the server URL from `--server` when given, and otherwise from `AF_URL`. An empty `AF_URL` counts as unset
accept as the server an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host and an optional path prefix. It drops one trailing `/` and sends API requests to `<url>/api/v1/…`

criteria.condition: the server URL is not absolute, is not `http` or `https`, has no host, or carries a query, a fragment or user info
criteria.action: refuse with a usage error that names `--server` or `AF_URL` (whichever gave the URL) and the rule broken, and send nothing
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.condition: a service command runs with neither `--server` nor a non-empty `AF_URL`
criteria.action: refuse with a usage error whose message names `--server` and `AF_URL`, and also `--local` for `triage` and `fix`, and send nothing
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2, `error.fix_hint` `{flag: "--server", env: "AF_URL"}`

criteria.condition: the server URL is `http` and its host is not loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`)
criteria.action: raise the warning `server_insecure` and continue the command
criteria.contract: envelope `warnings` contains code `server_insecure`

requirements.title: The hub credential
requirements.rationale: `~/.af/config.toml` is the only credential source named by PRD 01 and PRD 03. A bearer token must never leak or reach another host.

criteria.action: send every service request with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. The credential is the top-level string key `token` of `~/.af/config.toml`, where `~` is the home directory `os.UserHomeDir` reports. Every other key in the file is ignored

criteria.condition: the home directory cannot be found, or the credential file exists but cannot be read (permission denied, a directory, or a read error)
criteria.action: fail before any request with a message naming the path
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `io`; no request is sent

criteria.condition: the credential file does not exist, or its `token` is missing, is not a string, or is empty
criteria.action: fail before any request with a message naming the file and saying to run `af login --token-file FILE` or `afc login`
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `auth`, `error.fix_hint` `{suggest: "af login --token-file FILE"}`; no request is sent

criteria.condition: the credential file does not parse as TOML, or the credential holds a line break or a control character
criteria.action: fail before any request with a message naming the file
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `config`; no request is sent

criteria.condition: on Unix, the credential file has any group or other permission bit set
criteria.action: raise the warning `credential_file_permissions` naming the file, and continue the command
criteria.contract: envelope `warnings` contains code `credential_file_permissions`

criteria.action: for any credential and any workspace PAT, keep that secret out of stdout, stderr, the `--output` file, the events and `--emit-events`, every error message and every warning
criteria.contract: a sentinel credential and a sentinel PAT are absent from all four outputs

criteria.action: send the credential only to the host of the server URL, and to no other host

requirements.title: Storing a credential with af login
requirements.rationale: `af login` writes afc's file, so it must check the credential first and change only the value of `token`.

criteria.action:
read the credential from the `--token-file` file, or from stdin for `-`, and never from the command line. It then runs these steps in order, stopping at the first that fails and writing nothing:
1. read the credential
2. find the server
3. check the existing credential file
4. check the credential with the service
5. write the file
A token file that is missing or cannot be read, or stdin that cannot be read, fails with a message naming the path or stdin
criteria.contract: an unreadable source gives status `failed`, exit code 1, category `io`

criteria.condition: the trimmed credential is empty, spans more than one line, holds a control character, or is longer than 4096 bytes
criteria.action: refuse with a usage error naming `--token-file`, and write nothing
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.condition: an existing credential file cannot be read, does not parse as TOML, or has no top-level `token = "…"` or `token = '…'` line before any table header, where the value is a one-line string optionally followed by a comment
criteria.action: fail without sending the check request and without changing the file. For a layout problem, the message names the file, says its layout is not the one `af` expects, and says that `afc login` or an edit fixes it
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1; category `io` when unreadable, and `config` when the file does not parse or has the wrong layout; the file's bytes are unchanged

criteria.condition: the local checks pass
criteria.action: send `GET /api/v1/workspaces` with the new credential, and accept the credential on any 2xx answer

criteria.condition: the service answers the check with 401
criteria.action: fail with a message saying that the service refused this credential, and write nothing
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `auth`; the credential file is unchanged or still absent

criteria.condition: the check gets any answer other than 2xx or 401, a transport error, or runs past the request bound
criteria.action: fail as 16-REQ-6 maps the answer, with a message saying the credential could not be checked (not that it was refused), and write nothing
criteria.contract: a 502 gives status `failed`, exit code 1, category `hub`, `retryable` true; the credential file is unchanged

criteria.condition: the service accepts the credential
criteria.action:
write `~/.af/config.toml` through a temporary file in `~/.af` that is renamed over the old file, with file mode 0600.
- With no existing file, it creates `~/.af` with mode 0700 when missing and writes the single line `token = "<credential>"`.
- With an existing file, it replaces only the value on the `token` line with the credential as a TOML basic string, and keeps every other byte.
Its result never contains the credential
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit code 0, result `{credential_file, server}`

criteria.condition: creating `~/.af`, writing, syncing or closing the temporary file, or renaming it fails
criteria.action: fail with a message naming the path, remove the temporary file, and leave any existing credential file as it was
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `io`; the existing file's bytes are unchanged

requirements.title: Requests and how answers map
requirements.rationale: Scripts need the exit code and category of every failure to be predictable, and a bearer token must never follow a redirect.

criteria.action:
run its local checks in this order, and report the first that fails. It sends a request only after all of them pass:
1. the mode and flags (a missing or doubled mode, a refused or unknown flag, a malformed flag value)
2. the positional arguments and the input, including reading stdin, `af login`'s token file and the PAT file
3. the server URL
4. the credential, or for `af login` the existing credential file
criteria.contract: an invocation with several local mistakes reports the first in this order

criteria.action:
send every request with these headers, and any body as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`:
- `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`
- `User-Agent: af/<version>`, with the version from `App.Identity`
- `Accept: application/json`, or `Accept: text/event-stream` on the event stream

apply these bounds:
- each request other than the event stream lasts at most 2 minutes, or the command's remaining `--timeout` when that is shorter
- at most 8 MiB of a response body is read
- `--timeout` has no default limit on any client command
criteria.contract: a request past its bound fails as 16-REQ-6.5 maps it: category `service`, `retryable` true; a body past 8 MiB fails category `service`, `retryable` false

criteria.condition: the service answers with a 3xx redirect
criteria.action: not follow the redirect, send no request to its target, and treat the 3xx as the answer
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `service`, `retryable` false

criteria.condition: the service answers a request with a non-2xx status, a transport error occurs, the 2-minute bound runs out, or the body is too large or is not the expected JSON
criteria.action:
map the answer as follows:

| Answer | Status | Category | Retryable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `usage` | `usage` | false |
| 401 | `failed` | `auth` | false |
| 404 | `usage` | `usage` | false |
| 409 | `failed` | `conflict` | false |
| 422 | `failed` | `auth` | false |
| 502 | `failed` | `hub` | true |
| 500 | `failed` | `service` | false |
| 503, 504 and any other 5xx | `failed` | `service` | true |
| any other 4xx (including 405, 413 and 415) | `failed` | `service` | false |
| a transport error, or the bound running out | `failed` | `service` | true |
| a body too large or not the expected JSON | `failed` | `service` | false |
criteria.contract: the exit code follows the status: 2 for `usage` and 1 for `failed`; `error.category` and `error.retryable` are as in the table

criteria.action:
word failure messages as follows:
- in general, the service's `error.message` followed by its `error.code` in parentheses, or "the service answered <status>" when the body has neither
- for a transport error, also name the server URL and its source (`--server` or `AF_URL`)
- for a 404, name the job id or workspace slug asked for, and say it does not exist or hub does not let the caller see it
criteria.contract: `error.message` holds the text described

criteria.action:
attach these fix hints:
- `{suggest: "af login --token-file FILE"}` to a 401
- `{suggest: "af workspace subscribe <slug> --hub-token-file FILE"}` to a 404 on a workspace route, and to a 409 `not_subscribed` or `token_unreadable`
- `{flag: "--hub-token-file"}` to a 422
criteria.contract: `error.fix_hint` as listed

criteria.action: carry the service's JSON documents into its results as received, so that fields `af` does not know survive, and read only the fields it needs

requirements.title: Queuing a job with --workspace
requirements.rationale: The service decides which issue URLs it accepts, and the client must send input that fits the service's limits.

criteria.condition: `af triage <input> --workspace <slug>` runs
criteria.action:
turn the input into the request by the first matching rule:
1. `-` reads stdin and is sent as `text`
2. any `http://` or `https://` URL is sent as `issue`, the trimmed URL string, unclassified and without consulting any forge variable
3. a positive integer, optionally with a leading `#`, is sent as `issue`, a JSON number
4. `<path>#<N>`, where `<path>` is two or more `/`-separated segments of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, is sent as `issue`, the string
5. an existing regular file is sent as `file: {name: <base name>, content}`
6. anything else is sent as `text`

criteria.condition: `af fix --workspace` gets an input that matches none of rules 2, 3 and 4
criteria.action: refuse with a usage error saying that with `--workspace`, `af fix` takes an issue: `N`, `#N`, `owner/repo#N` or an issue URL
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2; no request is sent

criteria.condition: the text or file content is empty after trimming, holds a NUL byte or is not valid UTF-8; or the named file is a directory or cannot be read
criteria.action: refuse before any request
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2 for empty, NUL, invalid UTF-8 or a directory; status `failed`, exit code 1, category `io` for an unreadable file

criteria.condition: text or file content is longer than `MaxInputBytes` (131072)
criteria.action: cut the content at a UTF-8 boundary so that the content plus the truncation marker is at most `MaxInputBytes`, set `input.truncated`, and raise the warning `input_truncated`
criteria.contract: the sent content's length is at most 131072 bytes; envelope `input.truncated` is true

criteria.system: af triage and af fix in service mode
criteria.action:
report in the envelope's `input`:
- `kind`: `issue`, `file`, `text` or `stdin`
- `origin`: the URL for rule 2, the absolute file path for rule 5, and `""` otherwise
- `truncated`

criteria.system: af triage and af fix in service mode
criteria.action: post the body to `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/triage` or `/fix`, with the slug path-escaped. The `--context` values go as `context` in their order, and `context` is absent when there are none

criteria.condition: the service answers the queue request with 202
criteria.system: af triage and af fix in service mode
criteria.action:
record at once the artifact `{kind: "job", name: <id>, url: <server>/api/v1/jobs/<id>}`, then act on `--wait`:
- without it: finish with status `done`, result `{job, envelope: null}`, a summary naming the job and the workspace, and `next` `af jobs watch <id>` (with `--server <url>` when the server came from the flag)
- with it: follow the job as 16-REQ-9 and 16-REQ-10 describe
criteria.contract: without `--wait`, exit code 0

criteria.condition: the service answers the queue request with 409 `duplicate_job`
criteria.system: af triage and af fix in service mode
criteria.action: fail, carrying the service's message, which names the open job
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `conflict`, `retryable` false

requirements.title: Workspace subscriptions and job commands
requirements.rationale: A person must be able to subscribe workspaces and list, inspect, answer, retry and cancel jobs from `af`.

criteria.condition: `af workspace subscribe <slug> --hub-token-file <file|-> [--prefix P]` runs
criteria.action: send `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` with `{hub_token}`, adding `label_prefix` only when `--prefix` is given. Both 201 and 200 count as success, and the summary says subscribed for 201 and replaced for 200
criteria.contract: exit code 0, result: the subscription view as received

criteria.condition: the `--hub-token-file` file or stdin cannot be read, or its trimmed content is empty, multi-line, holds a control character, or is longer than 4096 bytes
criteria.action: fail before any request, naming the file or stdin for a read failure and `--hub-token-file` for a content rule
criteria.contract: for a read failure, status `failed`, exit code 1, category `io`; for a content rule, status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.action:
implement these subcommands, each taking the slug as a required, path-escaped positional argument where it applies:
- `list` sends `GET /api/v1/workspaces` and returns `{workspaces}`
- `get <slug>` sends `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` and returns the subscription view
- `unsubscribe <slug>` sends `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` and returns `{slug}` on 204, with a summary saying the workspace's open jobs were cancelled
criteria.contract: exit code 0 on success; a 400 about the slug maps to `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.condition: `af jobs list [--workspace S] [--state S] [--cursor C]` runs
criteria.action: send `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{S}/jobs` when `--workspace` is given, and `GET /api/v1/jobs` otherwise. `--state` and `--cursor` pass through as the `state` and `cursor` query parameters only when given. When `next_cursor` is not null, `next` repeats the command with `--cursor <next_cursor>`
criteria.contract: exit code 0, result: the page `{jobs, next_cursor}`

criteria.action:
implement these subcommands:
- `get <id>` sends `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}`
- `cancel <id>` sends `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel`
- `retry <id> [--wait]` sends `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/retry` with body `{}`
- `answer <id> … [--wait]` sends `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/answer`
Without `--wait` each returns `{job, envelope: null}` with status `done`. With `--wait`, `answer` and `retry` record the job artifact and follow the job as 16-REQ-9 and 16-REQ-10 describe
criteria.contract: without `--wait`, exit code 0

criteria.condition: `af jobs answer` is given no answer, or more than one of positional text, `--context` and `--option`
criteria.action: refuse with a usage error, and send no request
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.action:
handle the two kinds of answer as follows:
- an `--option` value is uppercased and sent as `{option}`
- a text answer (positional or `--context`) must be non-empty after trimming. `af` first reads the job: text equal to an option id of the blocked question, ignoring case, is sent as that `{option}`, and any other text as `{answer}`
criteria.contract: empty text gives status `usage`, exit code 2

criteria.condition: a job command gets a 409 (`invalid_state`, `not_subscribed` or `token_unreadable`)
criteria.action: fail, carrying the service's message and the fix hint of 16-REQ-6.7
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `conflict`, `retryable` false

requirements.title: Following a job's event stream
requirements.rationale: End of file cannot tell the server's end from a dropped connection, so following resumes from the last seq and stops only when a fresh read says the job is at rest.

criteria.action:
read the stream as follows:
- request `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/events?since=<n>`, starting from 0, or from `--since` for `af jobs watch`
- frame events by `id:`, `event:` and `data:` lines and a blank line
- ignore comment lines and unknown fields
- accept lines of at most 1 MiB

drop any event whose `seq` is at most the last one delivered. Each delivered event is emitted as the `af` event `job_event`, whose data is the service's event document `{seq, ts, job_id, attempt, type, data}`
criteria.contract: `--emit-events` holds one `job_event` per delivered event

criteria.action: write each delivered event document to stderr as one line of compact JSON under `af jobs watch`, and write nothing to stderr under `--wait`
criteria.contract: under `watch`, stderr holds one JSON line per event, in `seq` order

criteria.action:
run in tries.
- A stream ends at end of file, on a dropped connection, on an unreadable frame, or after 60 s with no byte. `af` then reads `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}`.
- When that read says the job is at rest, following ends and the result is built.
- Otherwise `af` makes another try with `since` set to the last `seq` delivered

count a try as failed when it ends without the job at rest and delivers no new event, whatever ended it. That includes a 5xx or transport error on the events request or on the job read. A try that delivers a new event resets the count. Waits between tries are:
- 1 s after a try that delivered an event
- 1, 2, 4 and 8 s after the first, second, third and fourth failed try in a row
criteria.contract: the delay before each try, measured on an injected clock, is 1, 2, 4 or 8 s after the 1st to 4th failed try in a row, and 1 s after a try that delivered an event

criteria.condition: the fifth try in a row fails
criteria.action: stop following without a further wait. The message names the job and says it may still be running, and `next` is `af jobs watch <id> --since <last seq>` (with `--server <url>` when the server came from the flag)
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `hub` when the last failure was a 502 and `service` otherwise, `retryable` true

criteria.condition: during following, the events request or the job read gets a 401, a 404, a 3xx or a 4xx other than those
criteria.action: stop following at once, with no further try, and map the answer as 16-REQ-6 says
criteria.contract: status, exit code and category as 16-REQ-6.5 maps the answer

criteria.action: for any sequence of stream cuts and duplicate frames, resume a stream cut after event k with `since=k`, and deliver every event of the job exactly once in ascending `seq` order
criteria.contract: `--emit-events` holds each event's `job_event` exactly once, in order

requirements.title: The outcome of following a job
requirements.rationale: `--wait` must exit with the job's own outcome, and interrupting `af` must never cancel shared work.

criteria.condition: following finds the job at rest
criteria.action:
read the job with its attempts, then fetch `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/attempts/{n}/envelope` for the highest-numbered attempt whose state is not `queued` or `running`.
- A 404 leaves the envelope null.
- Any other failure leaves it null and raises the warning `attempt_envelope_unavailable`
criteria.contract: result `{job, envelope}`

criteria.action: append the attempt envelope's warnings to `af`'s own. Its artifacts, side effects, `next` and usage are not copied, `af`'s `usage` stays the no-brain usage, and following adds no `next` of its own on reaching rest

criteria.condition: the job at rest is `done`
criteria.action: take the envelope's `result.status`, which is `done` or `unverified`, and use `done` when `result` is null
criteria.contract: exit code 0 for `done`, 4 for `unverified`

criteria.condition: the job at rest is `blocked`
criteria.action: end `needs_human`, with the blocked question and its option labels in order
criteria.contract: status `needs_human`, exit code 3, `needs_human.resume` `{argv: ["af","jobs","answer",<id>,"--wait"], flag: "--context"}`, with `--server <url>` added to argv when the server came from the flag

criteria.condition: the job at rest is `failed`
criteria.action: take the envelope's `result.status`, which is `failed`, `unverified` or `usage`. A failure carries `result.error`'s category, message, retryable flag and fix hint, and is category `internal` when `result.error` is null
criteria.contract: exit code 1 for `failed`, 4 for `unverified`, 2 for `usage`

criteria.condition: the job at rest is `cancelled`
criteria.action: fail with a message saying the job was cancelled on the service, and ignore the attempt envelope's category
criteria.contract: status `failed`, exit code 1, category `job_cancelled`, `retryable` false

criteria.condition: `af` is interrupted by SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, or its `--timeout` runs out, while following
criteria.action: stop following without sending any cancel request. Only on this path, add `next` entries `af jobs watch <id>` and `af jobs cancel <id>` (each with `--server <url>` when the server came from the flag). The job artifact, which was recorded before following started, stays in the envelope
criteria.contract: the shell's failure: category `cancelled` for a signal or `timeout` for the bound; `artifacts` names the job

execution_paths.title: A person logs in and subscribes a workspace

steps.action: runs `af login --token-file -` with a hub token on stdin and `AF_URL` set
checks the token with `GET /api/v1/workspaces` on the service, which answers 200
writes `~/.af/config.toml` with mode 0600 through a temporary file and a rename, and returns `{credential_file, server}` with exit 0
runs `af workspace subscribe widgets --hub-token-file f`
sends `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/widgets` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `{hub_token}`
validates the PAT against fakehub, stores the subscription, and answers 201 with the subscription view
writes a `done` envelope carrying the subscription view and exits 0

execution_paths.title: A fix job is queued and waited on until it is done

steps.action: runs `af fix 42 --workspace widgets --wait`
runs the local checks in order, then posts `{issue: 42}` to `POST /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/fix`
creates the job and answers 202 with the job document
records the job artifact and reads `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/events?since=0`, emitting each event as `job_event`
returns a `done` envelope for attempt 1, and the stream ends with `job_state` `at_rest: true`
reads the job, finds it at rest, and fetches `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/attempts/1/envelope`
writes an envelope with `result.job.state` `done` and `result.envelope` set to attempt 1's envelope, and exits 0

execution_paths.title: A blocked triage job is answered through its resume argv

steps.action: runs `af triage 42 --workspace widgets --wait`
queues the job, and the fake runner ends attempt 1 `needs_human` with options A and B, so the job becomes blocked
follows the job to rest and exits 3 with `needs_human.resume` `{argv: ["af","jobs","answer",<id>,"--wait"], flag: "--context"}`
runs the resume argv with `--context B` appended
reads the job, matches `B` to an option id, and posts `{option: "B"}` to `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/answer`
answers 202 and starts attempt 2, whose runner receives option B's label as the answer
follows attempt 2 to rest and exits with the attempt envelope's exit code

execution_paths.title: A fix with no mode is refused before anything happens

steps.action: runs `af fix https://github.com/o/r/issues/1` with neither `--local` nor `--workspace`
reads the words before parsing flags, and finds no mode
writes a usage envelope naming `--workspace`, `--server`/`AF_URL` and `--local`, sends no request to the forge or the service, creates no `.agent-fox/run/` directory, and exits 2

execution_paths.title: A local triage runs as before and suggests a local fix

steps.action: runs `af triage <issue url> --local --dir <dir>` with `AF_URL` pointing at a closed port
chooses local mode and hands the invocation to the local triage command
resolves the issue from the forge, creates the run directory, and runs the brain to a confirmed diagnosis
writes the envelope with `next` `af fix <issue url> --dir <dir> --local`, sends no request to the agent-fox service, and exits 0

execution_paths.title: Watching a job resumes after a dropped stream

steps.action: runs `af jobs watch <id> --emit-events events.jsonl`
records the job artifact and reads `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/events?since=0`
sends events 1 to k, then cuts the connection
reads the job, finds it not at rest, waits 1 s, and requests `events?since=k`
replays a duplicate frame, then sends the remaining events and a final `job_state` with `at_rest: true`
writes each event once to stderr and to events.jsonl in `seq` order, fetches the final attempt envelope, and exits with the job's status
